teams.name: Cardinals
teams.subhead: 2026 training camp edition — Kyler Murray is gone, the presumptive starter is holding out, and the Mike LaFleur era begins with a three-man quarterback competition.

left.title: Front Office & Leadership
items: Gannon out, LaFleur in. A 3–14 collapse cost Jonathan Gannon his job and launched the Mike LaFleur era. Arizona is not pretending otherwise — national previews describe this camp under a single instruction: embrace the rebuild.

The Murray divorce. Arizona moved on from Kyler Murray, who signed with Minnesota for the veteran minimum — with the Cardinals still paying the remainder of his $36.5M guarantee for 2026. That is the price of a clean break.
Plan B didn't land either. The club struck out on both Malik Willis and Jimmy Garoppolo before settling on Gardner Minshew and spending a third-round pick on Carson Beck.
Camp: opened Wednesday, runs through Aug. 11 at State Farm Stadium. Arizona and Carolina were the first two teams in the league to fully report.

left.title: Trades & Major Transactions
items: DepartedKyler Murray, QB — to Minnesota, with Arizona absorbing the guaranteed money.
SignedQB Gardner Minshew, presumed as a backup rather than a solution.
SignedG Isaac Seumalo — three years, $31.5M, the clearest signal that the offensive line is being overhauled.
SignedWR/RS Devin Duvernay, a former All-Pro returner who takes both return jobs and adds a speed element on offense.
DraftQB Carson Beck (3rd round, signed his rookie deal July 22 as camp opened), RB Jeremiyah Love, and 2025 first-rounder DT Walter Nolen III now healthy after an injury-marred rookie year.

right.title: Player Updates & Camp Battles
items: HoldoutJacoby Brissett, QB. The presumptive starter skipped the entire offseason program seeking a new deal. His absence is why a three-man competition exists at all.
Carson Beck, QB (3rd round). Signed July 22 and thrown straight into a competition with Brissett and Minshew. A rookie starting Week 1 is a live possibility.
Jeremiyah Love, RB. The rookie some analysts call the best player on the roster, with a projected 1,000-yard, 10-touchdown ceiling. The starting running back job is genuinely open.
Walter Nolen III, DT. The 2025 first-rounder lost his rookie season to injuries; healthy now, he's the defense's most important developmental case.
Isaac Seumalo, G. The veteran anchor of a line being rebuilt around him.
Devin Duvernay, WR/RS. Immediate upgrade on both return units — the fastest way for a rebuilding roster to steal field position.

right.title: Camp Calendar
items: Training camp, State Farm Stadium, Glendale
Brissett (if he reports) vs. Minshew vs. Beck
Nolen's health; Seumalo settling the interior line

right.title: The Bottom Line
items: Arizona is paying a quarterback $36.5M to play in Minnesota, and the man supposed to replace him hasn't shown up. That is the 2026 Cardinals in one sentence. Mike LaFleur inherits a genuine rebuild — a rookie third-rounder who might have to start, a running back who could be the roster's best player, and a first-round defensive tackle finally healthy. Seumalo and Duvernay are the only signings that look like wins today. The rest is development, and everybody in the building knows it.

teams.name: Falcons
teams.subhead: 2026 training camp edition — a new head coach, a nearly new front office, and a quarterback competition nobody saw coming a year ago.

left.title: Front Office & Leadership
items: Kevin Stefanski takes over. Atlanta opens its first camp under the former Browns head coach, with a coaching staff and front office that are largely new — one of the most complete organizational resets in the league this offseason.
The mandate is the quarterback. Stefanski inherits a QB room that now includes both Tua Tagovailoa and Michael Penix Jr., and settling it is the defining task of his first summer.
Roster philosophy: fix the two things that cost Atlanta games — pass rush and pass-catching depth — with volume rather than one headline contract.

left.title: Trades & Major Transactions
items: SignedTua Tagovailoa, QB arrives to compete with Michael Penix Jr. for the starting job — the storyline every national preview leads with.
SignedRT Jawaan Taylor from Kansas City, then traded for his former Chiefs teammate OT Wanya Morris — the right side of the line rebuilt in a week.
SignedEDGE Azeez Ojulari (from Philadelphia), EDGE Cameron Thomas and EDGE Samson Ebukam — three additions to a rush that needed all three.
SignedWR Jahan Dotson and WR Olamide Zaccheaus (from Chicago); drafted WR Zachariah Branch in the third round.
TradeAcquired S Sydney Brown and picks 122 and 215 from Philadelphia for picks 114 and 197 (March 20).
Re-signedTE Kyle Pitts on a new contract — the most notable retention of the offseason. K Nick Folk, 41, added along with a new punter; LS Liam McCullough stays.

right.title: Player Updates & Camp Battles
items: QB1 is the camp. Tagovailoa vs. Penix is a real competition, not a formality, and Stefanski's read on it will shape how the rest of the roster is used.
Kyle Pitts, TE. New deal in hand, and a Stefanski offense is historically friendly to a tight end who can win up the seam.
Jawaan Taylor & Wanya Morris, OT. Two Chiefs imports handed the right side of the line — continuity of scheme and familiarity with each other is the bet.
Zachariah Branch, WR (3rd round). The most explosive rookie in the class of additions; joins Dotson and Zaccheaus in a rebuilt receiver room.
Edge rotation, from scratch. Ojulari, Thomas and Ebukam were all signed to solve the same problem. Which two emerge is a genuine camp battle.
Nickel corner, open. Free-agent Darnay Holmes and trade acquisition Sydney Brown are both in the mix.

right.title: Latest Roster Moves
head: Move
Detail
items: Hired as head coach; staff and front office largely new
Signed to compete with Penix for QB1
Acquired by trade from Kansas City
Three edge rushers added in free agency
Receiver room rebuilt in FA and the draft
Acquired from Philadelphia with picks 122 and 215
Signed at 41 alongside a new punter

right.title: The Bottom Line
items: Atlanta blew it up at the top — new coach, new staff, new front office — and then spent the offseason buying the two things Stefanski's system cannot function without: a competent right side of the offensive line and enough pass rush to keep games close. The rest is the quarterback. Tagovailoa and Penix will settle it in camp, and whichever way Stefanski rules, it is the decision his tenure gets judged on. First practice is July 29.

teams.name: Ravens
teams.subhead: 2026 training camp edition — 18 years of John Harbaugh ended in January. Jesse Minter's first camp opens with Lamar Jackson learning a brand-new offense.

left.title: Front Office & Leadership
items: The Harbaugh era is over. Baltimore fired John Harbaugh after 18 seasons and a Super Bowl XLVII title; he was hired by the Giants days later on a five-year deal.
Jesse Minter takes over and reset the operation around himself. He called the Baltimore job "the one I wanted," and has made building a relationship with Lamar Jackson his first stated priority.
Declan Doyle runs the offense. Hired from Chicago, he is the NFL's youngest play-caller — and everything about camp routes through Jackson learning his system.
Minter's own assignment: fix a defense that finished 24th in 2025, which is what got the last staff fired.

left.title: Trades & Major Transactions
items: SignedTrey Hendrickson, EDGE — the marquee addition, and a fast pivot after Baltimore rescinded a trade for Maxx Crosby that would have cost 2026 first-round capital. The sequence drew criticism around the league.
SignedDL Calais Campbell — the veteran presence on a rebuilt front.
DraftG Vega Ioane (Penn State) in the first round, plus pass rusher Zion Young — a reworked offensive line and more juice off the edge.
Re-signedQB Tyler Huntley and CB Daryl Awuzie; OL Gwyn added on a one-year deal for depth.
LostTE Charlie Kolar to the Chargers — Smythe is expected to take over as the blocking tight end. TE Isaiah Likely followed Harbaugh to New York on a 3-year, $40M deal.

right.title: Player Updates & Camp Battles
items: Lamar Jackson, QB. Learning an entirely new system for the first time in years. Doyle's install, and how quickly the two of them find a shared language, is the defining question of Baltimore's season.
Timing with the pass catchers. Jackson's rhythm with Zay Flowers, Rashod Bateman, Mark Andrews and the young receivers has to be rebuilt inside a new scheme — and without Likely.
A reworked offensive line. Jackson's comfort behind it is a stated camp storyline; first-round guard Vega Ioane is expected to help immediately.
Trey Hendrickson, EDGE. Signed to be the pressure Baltimore's 24th-ranked defense never generated.
Calais Campbell, DL. Veteran anchor next to Hendrickson and Young in Minter's front.
Lamar arrived on time for the first Minter camp — a small thing that was, given the offseason, its own headline.

right.title: Latest Roster Moves
head: Move
Detail
items: Signed after the Crosby trade was rescinded
Fired after 18 seasons; hired by the Giants
Followed Harbaugh to New York, 3 yr / $40M
Signed with the Los Angeles Chargers

right.title: The Bottom Line
items: Baltimore did the hardest thing a stable franchise can do: it ended an 18-year marriage and started over on the sideline while keeping a former MVP at quarterback. Jesse Minter inherits the 24th-ranked defense he was hired to fix and hands the offense to the league's youngest play-caller. Hendrickson and Campbell make the front credible; Ioane makes the line better. But the season lives or dies on how fast Lamar Jackson learns Declan Doyle's language. The offseason was aggressive enough that missing the playoffs would count as failure.

teams.sources: ESPN (2026 Ravens training camp preview & free agency tracker) · NFL.com · BaltimoreRavens.com · Yahoo Sports (Ravens offseason takeaways) · The Baltimore Banner · Sports Illustrated.

teams.name: Bills
teams.subhead: 2026 training camp edition — nine seasons of Sean McDermott ended in January. Joe Brady is the head coach, the defense is switching fronts, and Josh Allen finally has a true WR1.

left.title: Front Office & Leadership
items: McDermott fired. Nine seasons, no Super Bowl, and a 33–30 overtime loss to Denver in the divisional round ended it. Buffalo announced the decision the following Monday.
Joe Brady promoted. The offensive coordinator got the job. He was candid about the cost: "I was broken" for McDermott and the assistants who were let go.
Beane elevated. GM Brandon Beane was promoted to president of football operations and oversaw the coaching search that landed on his own play-caller.
Scheme change on defense. The new coordinator brings a 3-4 base, a structural break from McDermott's 4-3 and one of several reasons ESPN describes this as an "extremely tough" camp.

left.title: Trades & Major Transactions
items: TradeDJ Moore acquired from Chicago for a 2026 second-round pick (Buffalo also received a 2026 fifth). Josh Allen finally gets a proven WR1 — and Moore reunites with Joe Brady, his offensive coordinator in Carolina.
SignedEDGE Bradley Chubb on a three-year deal — the marquee defensive addition for the new front.
SignedQB Kyle Allen (2 yr / $6.1M, from Detroit) — another former Bills backup, and a close friend of Josh Allen's.
LostT Ryan Van Demark to Minnesota after Buffalo declined to match an offer sheet; G David Edwards to New Orleans on a deal with $45M guaranteed.
Very little was left untouched for a franchise that had been among the league's most stable.

right.title: Player Updates & Camp Battles
items: Josh Allen, QB. Arguably no player in football carries more pressure into 2026. Nine years in, with a new head coach and a new scheme on the other side of the ball, his leadership through the transition is the point. His own words: there's a lot new, and "we'll really make our team during training camp."
DJ Moore, WR. The separator Buffalo has been missing, arriving into a system run by a coach who already knows how to use him.
Bradley Chubb, EDGE. Signed to give the new 3-4 front a genuine edge presence.
Dalton Kincaid, TE. The fourth-year tight end's career keeps getting interrupted — the left knee most recently. He is genuinely impactful when available; availability is the whole issue.
Defensive install. Moving from a 4-3 to a 3-4 mid-career for an entire roster is the hardest thing this team is attempting in August.
Offensive line, thinner. Van Demark and Edwards both left; interior depth is a live question.

right.title: Latest Roster Moves
head: Move
Detail
items: Promoted from OC to head coach
Trade with Chicago for a 2026 second
Promoted to president of football operations
Offer sheet from Minnesota not matched

right.title: The Bottom Line
items: Buffalo fired a coach who won a lot of regular-season games and never got to a Super Bowl, promoted the man who ran its offense, and handed the defense a new front to learn. Then it went out and got Josh Allen the No. 1 receiver he has never had. That is a franchise spending its remaining Allen years decisively rather than carefully. It is also a lot of change at once, which is exactly why the quarterback keeps saying the team gets made in camp.

teams.sources: ESPN (2026 Bills training camp preview & free agency tracker) · BuffaloBills.com · NFL.com · NBC News · NBC Sports · Bleacher Report.

teams.name: Panthers
teams.subhead: 2026 training camp edition — first playoff berth since 2017, the offseason's biggest edge contract, and a rebuild the league now describes as ahead of schedule.

left.title: Front Office & Leadership
items: Morgan went hunting for pass rush. The GM said quarterback pressure in 2025 was "not acceptable" and promised to be aggressive about it. He then wrote the largest edge contract of the offseason.

Canales hands off the play sheet. Offensive coordinator Brad Idzik takes over play-calling from the head coach — a real change in how this offense operates day to day, and the quietest big story of the camp.

Scheme fit was the sell. Jaelan Phillips thrived under Vic Fangio in Philadelphia, and Carolina runs a similar 3-4 with the flexibility to shift to a 4-3 — the front office's explicit reasoning for the price.
Camp readiness: Carolina and Arizona were the first two teams in the NFL to fully report for 2026 camp.

left.title: Trades & Major Transactions
items: SignedJaelan Phillips, EDGE — four years, $120M with $80M guaranteed, prised away from Philadelphia. He ranked ninth in the NFL in quarterback pressures (73) in 2025.
SignedDevin Lloyd, LB — three years, $45M, from Jacksonville.
SignedWR John Metchie III, reuniting with his college quarterback. In their last season together in 2021 he posted a team-high 96 catches for 1,142 yards and eight scores.
SignedQB Kenny Pickett to the backup job.
TradeQB Andy Dalton to Philadelphia on a three-year, $24.75M deal.
DraftSix of seven picks signed, including OT Monroe Freeling and WR Chris Brazzell.

right.title: Player Updates & Camp Battles
items: Bryce Young, QB. Career-best season — first time past 3,000 yards and 20 touchdown passes — and he led Carolina back to the playoffs. The counterargument is still on the stat sheet: EPA per dropback third-worst among qualified starters, QBR 25th. Year 4 is the verdict year.
Tetairoa McMillan, WR. Coming off an award-winning rookie season. His ascension is the offense's most likely leap.
A crowded receiver room. Xavier Legette, Chris Brazzell and Jimmy Horn Jr. are all competing for the snaps behind McMillan — chemistry with Young is the tiebreaker.
Jaelan Phillips, EDGE. $120M arrives to fix the pressure problem by himself if necessary.
Devin Lloyd, LB. Adds range and downhill play behind the new front.
Offensive line health is the open question — injuries have muddied how the front five sorts out.

right.title: The Bottom Line
items: Carolina got to January a year early, and Dan Morgan responded by paying full price for the one thing that keeps you there: pressure. Phillips and Lloyd cost $165M combined, and both fit a front that can flip between 3-4 and 4-3. The offense is the more interesting experiment — Brad Idzik now calls it, McMillan is ready for more, and Bryce Young has to prove that a playoff season was a floor rather than a ceiling. The underlying numbers still say the jury is out.

teams.sources: ESPN (2026 Panthers training camp preview & free agency tracker) · Panthers.com · NFL.com · Sports Illustrated · Last Word on Sports.

teams.name: Bears
teams.subhead: 2026 training camp edition — Caleb Williams reported healthy and in peak condition; veterans arrive Tuesday, July 28. New safety tandem debuts. Can defense pair elite takeaways with actual pass rush?

left.title: Front Office & Leadership
items: Poles & Johnson locked in step. GM Ryan Poles' extension aligned him with head coach Ben Johnson — both under contract through the 2029 season, giving Halas Hall its cleanest continuity window in a decade.

Coaching staff deepened. Press Taylor promoted to offensive coordinator (Jaguars OC, 2022–24); Ben Johnson still calls offensive plays. New hires: Eric Studesville (RBs coach), Will Lawing (offensive analyst), Isaiah Ford (OC coach; ex-NFL receiver). Dennis Allen returns as DC; Richard Hightower anchors special teams.

Stadium file still open. President/CEO Kevin Warren reiterated the Arlington Heights project — pitched as zero state construction dollars — while the club keeps doing due diligence on a Hammond, Ind. site, where enabling legislation has already passed. Springfield has signaled the project isn't a 2026 priority.

Caleb extension groundwork. Poles can't formally negotiate with Williams until after year three, but the Bears have set the table for a long-term deal next offseason. The green light is Williams' to earn in 2026.

left.title: Trades & Major Transactions
items: TradeDJ Moore to Buffalo. Moore plus a 2026 fifth-rounder shipped to the Bills for a 2026 second-round pick. Widely graded a win-win: Buffalo gets Josh Allen a proven separator, Chicago banks a top-64 asset and clears the WR room for its young pass catchers.
TradeGarrett Bradbury from New England for a 2027 fifth-rounder — the answer at center after Drew Dalman's abrupt retirement this offseason.
SignedDevin Bush, LB — three years, $30M. The tone-setter in a faster, more aggressive front seven; priority defensive move.
SignedCoby Bryant, S — three years, three-time Pro Bowler fresh off Seattle's Super Bowl LX championship (4 INTs in 2025). Starts opposite rookie Dillon Thieneman in all-new safety tandem.
SignedNeville Gallimore, DT (2 yr), Cam Lewis, CB (2 yr; seven-year Bills veteran), Kalif Raymond, WR (reunites with Ben Johnson from Jacksonville), Braxton Jones, LT (1 yr, up to $10M).
Re-signedDL Daniel Hardy (2 yr), LB D'Marco Jackson (2 yr), QB Case Keenum (2 yr), DB Elijah Hicks (1 yr), OL Jordan McFadden (1 yr).
CapCole Kmet and Jonah Jackson contracts reworked for space; Kmet now a lock on the 53 with Moore's targets up for grabs.

left.title: Rumor Mill
items: SpeculationTrade-deadline swing at edge rusher is the most persistent national projection — the 2025 defense led the NFL in takeaways but ranked poorly rushing the passer and stopping the run.
SpeculationESPN's Benjamin Solak floated a blockbuster for Colts RB Jonathan Taylor in his season-prediction slate. Analyst forecast, not a reported conversation.
SpeculationKyler Gordon's standing is the quiet camp storyline — five games played in 2025 and a soft-tissue cascade have him fighting for his place in Year 2 of a 3-year, $40M deal.

left.title: What's Next
items: Rookies & quarterbacks report to Halas Hall
at Carolina Panthers — season opener on the road

right.title: Player Updates & Camp Battles
items: Caleb Williams, QB. Reported to camp Saturday in peak physical condition, having set franchise single-season record with 3,942 passing yards in Year 2. Johnson has set higher completion-percentage bar for Year 3; Williams has responded with excellent offseason work. The extension Poles drafted can be signed next offseason if Williams continues his trajectory.
Rome Odunze, WR. The stress fracture in his left foot healed without surgery. With Moore gone he's the presumptive WR1 — but Luther Burden III is chasing that title.
Colston Loveland, TE. Finished ninth among TEs at 713 yards in a limited rookie role; projection models have him leading Chicago in receiving with 1,000-yard upside.
Ozzy Trapilo, OT. Patellar tendon injury in the Wild Card round — expected to open the season on PUP, freeing a roster spot.
Left tackle battle. Braxton Jones took every first-team spring rep (44 career starts, healthy) and leads Jedrick Wills Jr. and Theo Benedet for Week 1.
Jaylon Johnson, CB. Make-or-break year: missed 10 games in 2025, and his 4-yr/$76M deal has no guarantees left after this season with an out following 2026.

Dillon Thieneman, S. No. 25 overall from Oregon: 4.35 forty-time, 41-inch vertical, elite ballhawk rated draft's 11th-best pick overall by ESPN. Starts opposite Coby Bryant in all-new safety tandem tasked with complementing last year's league-leading takeaway rate.
Logan Jones, C. Round 2 pick addressing center void left by Dalman's retirement; immediate need filler with upside.
Malik Muhammad, CB. Round 4 corner competing opposite Jaylon Johnson; must help stabilize a secondary needing depth.
Kyle Monangai, RB & Austin Booker, EDGE headline a rising sophomore class expected to absorb real snaps.

right.title: Latest Roster Moves
head: Move
Detail
items: 4-year deal — last unsigned 2026 draft pick, in before camp
1st-rounder and OL Logan Jones signed rookie deals
Scotty Miller and Kyron Hudson added to camp roster
RB Salvon Ahmed; ex-Packers DB Anthony Johnson Jr.
Placed on international player exemption — doesn't count vs. 90
Departed to Atlanta in free agency

right.title: The Bottom Line
items: Chicago built defensively for scheme continuity over splashes: Coby Bryant's Super Bowl pedigree at safety, Devin Bush's speed at linebacker, Dillon Thieneman's ballhawking. The offense is unmistakably Ben Johnson's now, built around Caleb Williams (who reported in peak condition), Colston Loveland, Rome Odunze, and Luther Burden instead of DJ Moore. The central question: can Dennis Allen's defense pair 2025's league-best 33 takeaways with an actual pass rush? Chicago ranked poorly rushing the passer last year despite the pickoffs. If the new safety tandem and faster linebacker corps lift that dimension, the Bears have a legitimate playoff trajectory. Williams' extension awaits if he executes Johnson's vision in Year 3.

teams.name: Bengals
teams.subhead: 2026 training camp edition — three straight years out of the playoffs ended the patience. Cincinnati spent a top-10 pick on a defense worthy of Joe Burrow.

left.title: Front Office & Leadership
items: Aggression, finally. After three straight postseason misses, the front office overhauled the defense specifically to show Burrow the organization is serious about winning while he is in his prime — the exact criticism leveled at Cincinnati for years.
Zac Taylor enters Year 8 under real pressure. The floor for this season is a playoff berth; anything less is difficult to survive.
The philosophy shift: Cincinnati traded premium draft capital for a proven star rather than accumulating picks — a departure from how this front office has historically operated.
Camp: July 26 – Aug. 16 at the team's downtown Cincinnati headquarters.

left.title: Trades & Major Transactions
items: TradeDexter Lawrence II from the Giants for the No. 10 overall pick — one for one. A three-time Pro Bowl nose tackle becomes the anchor of the defensive front.
SignedDT Jonathan Allen — two-time Pro Bowler, lining up next to Lawrence. The interior went from a weakness to the strength of the roster in one offseason.
SignedEDGE Boye Mafe from the Super Bowl champion Seahawks.
SignedS Bryan Cook — secondary help behind the new front.
DraftEDGE Cashius Howell in the second round, rounding out the rush rotation.

right.title: Player Updates & Camp Battles
items: Joe Burrow, QB. The whole plan is built around him being healthy and in his prime. The offense was never the problem — the question ESPN poses about this camp is whether a better defense can finally complement him.
Ja'Marr Chase, WR. Returns as the centerpiece of an attack that has carried Cincinnati by itself for three seasons.
Dexter Lawrence II, DT. The most important addition on the roster and the reason a first-round pick is playing elsewhere.
Jonathan Allen, DT. Pairs with Lawrence to give the Bengals two Pro Bowl-caliber interior linemen for the first time in years.
Boye Mafe & Cashius Howell, EDGE. The veteran and the rookie splitting a rebuilt rush rotation.
WatchNational coverage this month has flagged messaging around Burrow heading into camp as something to monitor — the pressure on this season is not being hidden.

right.title: Latest Roster Moves
head: Move
Detail
items: Acquired from the Giants for pick No. 10
Sent to New York in the Lawrence deal

right.title: The Bottom Line
items: For three years the criticism of Cincinnati was identical every offseason: an elite quarterback, an elite receiver, and a defense that wasted them. This spring the Bengals answered it in the most direct way available — a top-10 pick for Dexter Lawrence, Jonathan Allen beside him, Mafe and Howell off the edge. Zac Taylor's eighth season now has no excuses attached to it. If this defense is merely average, Burrow and Chase should do the rest.

teams.sources: ESPN (2026 Bengals training camp preview) · Bengals.com free agency tracker · Bleacher Report · Newsweek · Sports Illustrated / All Bengals · Heavy.com.

teams.name: Browns
teams.subhead: 2026 training camp edition — Myles Garrett is a Ram, Todd Monken is the new head coach, and the quarterback job is genuinely undecided.

left.title: Front Office & Leadership
items: Todd Monken takes over. The former Ravens offensive coordinator (three seasons) returns to Cleveland, where he served one year as OC in 2019. His predecessor, Kevin Stefanski, is now the head coach in Atlanta.
Berry accepted reality. Trading Myles Garrett was the front office formally acknowledging the franchise is rebuilding — not retooling.
No hard feelings. Monken has publicly said he holds no grudge over the offseason drama that preceded Garrett's exit.
The assignment: settle the quarterback position, and convert the Garrett return into a young defensive core.

left.title: Trades & Major Transactions
items: TradeMyles Garrett to the Rams — the biggest deal of the 2026 offseason. Cleveland got back EDGE Jared Verse, a 25-year-old two-time Pro Bowler, plus multiple picks including a 2027 first-rounder. Verse's inclusion is what moved the needle.
Verse is the centerpiece. Getting a young, proven edge rusher rather than pure draft capital is the difference between a teardown and a reset.
Draft additions including OL Spencer Fano and LB Carson Schwesinger have been highlighted as reasons for optimism in an otherwise grim year.
ContextGarrett trade rumors had swirled for months, tying Cleveland to Philadelphia as well before the Rams closed it in June.

right.title: Player Updates & Camp Battles
items: QB1Deshaun Watson vs. Shedeur Sanders is the camp. Monken called it too close to call at the end of spring workouts — which is either honest or ominous depending on your view.
Deshaun Watson, QB. Healthy after two Achilles surgeries that cost him all of 2025. He has played just 19 games since 2022 between suspension and injury.
Shedeur Sanders, QB. The other half of a battle that will determine whether Cleveland believes it has a franchise quarterback at all — the actual point of the exercise.
Jared Verse, EDGE. Two Pro Bowls at 25, now the best player on the roster and the face of what Cleveland got for Garrett.
Spencer Fano, OL & Carson Schwesinger, LB. Young pieces expected to play immediately in a rebuilding year.
Defensive line, post-Garrett. Replacing a reigning Defensive Player of the Year is not a job one player does; the whole rotation gets rebuilt around Verse.

right.title: Latest Roster Moves
head: Move
Detail
items: Hired as head coach from Baltimore
Part of the Garrett package from the Rams
Traded to the Los Angeles Rams
Left; now head coach of the Atlanta Falcons

right.title: The Bottom Line
items: Cleveland stopped pretending. Trading the reigning Defensive Player of the Year for a 25-year-old Pro Bowler and a 2027 first is the cleanest possible admission that this roster needs years, not moves. Todd Monken's first camp is really a referendum on two quarterbacks — a healthy Deshaun Watson who has played 19 games in four years, and Shedeur Sanders. If neither answers it, the Browns will have spent the Garrett capital to find out, which was the point.

teams.sources: ESPN (2026 Browns training camp preview; Garrett trade reporting) · Dawgs By Nature · 247Sports · Sports Illustrated / Browns Digest · Cleveland Browns Community.

teams.name: Cowboys
teams.subhead: 2026 training camp edition — a new defensive coordinator, a rebuilt front, and a franchise-tagged receiver reporting to Oxnard without a holdout.

left.title: Front Office & Leadership
items: Eberflus fired. Dallas dismissed defensive coordinator Matt Eberflus after one of the worst defensive seasons in franchise history and hired Eagles defensive backs coach Christian Parker to replace him.
Defensive staff turnover. Parker brought in his own assistants; the offensive staff stayed largely intact, adding only Kyle Fuller (asst. OL/QC) and Stephen Bravo-Brown (asst. WRs).
Front office unchanged. Calls for outside leadership — including fan speculation about Troy Aikman — go nowhere. Dallas remains a family business, and any succession runs through Stephen Jones.
Year 2 under Schottenheimer. The first season had highs, but missing the playoffs again made it a clear disappointment.

left.title: Trades & Major Transactions
items: TradeRashan Gary from Green Bay (March 9) for a 2027 fourth-rounder — the headline answer to a pass rush that had much to prove.
TradeOsa Odighizuwa to San Francisco for a 2026 third-round pick (No. 92).
SignedS Jalen Thompson — three years, up to $33M, the biggest free-agent commitment of the offseason.
SignedQB Sam Howell from Philadelphia, plus one-year deals for a former Charger (up to $3M) and a former Ram ($5.5M).

Parsons haulThe 2025 Micah Parsons trade closed out through this draft: first-round picks in 2026 and 2027 plus DL Kenny Clark became, among others, edge Malachi Lawrence (23rd), CB Devin Moore (114th) and DL LT Overton (137th). Stephen Jones says the club feels "really good" about it.
LostWR Jalen Tolbert to Miami; S Thomas to Indianapolis.

right.title: Player Updates & Camp Battles
items: George Pickens, WR. Playing on the franchise tag at $27.3M after career highs of 93 catches, 1,429 yards and nine touchdowns. He plans to participate fully — no holdout — and joined Dak Prescott's Park City workout with CeeDee Lamb and the skill group. Dallas wants a second season of evidence before committing long term.
Dak Prescott, QB. The offense was the functional half of 2025 and returns essentially intact, with Lamb and Pickens both in camp.
The new defense. ESPN's framing of this camp is blunt: how fast can Parker's scheme get up to speed? Dallas is installing a new system with a substantially new front.
Rashan Gary, EDGE. The pass rush's centerpiece addition, acquired to replace production Dallas has been chasing since the Parsons trade.
Kenny Clark & the interior. Clark plus rookie LT Overton reset a defensive line that also shipped out Odighizuwa.
Malachi Lawrence, EDGE (23rd overall). The most direct on-field return from the Parsons deal, arriving into an immediate role.

right.title: The Bottom Line
items: Dallas spent 2025 proving that a very good offense cannot outrun a historically bad defense. The response was surgical rather than sweeping: fire the coordinator, import Gary, spend the Parsons capital on the front seven, and let the offense alone. The best news of the summer is the least dramatic — George Pickens is showing up, tagged and unhappy-free, throwing with Prescott in Utah. If Christian Parker's install takes, this roster is a playoff team. If it doesn't, the questions move up a floor.

teams.name: Broncos
teams.subhead: 2026 training camp edition — AFC #1 seed with a bold Jaylen Waddle trade, Bo Nix's health critical, and Super Bowl expectations met with urgency.

left.title: Front Office & Leadership
items: 14-3 and seeded #1 in the AFC. Denver earned the top seed, beat Buffalo 33-30 in the Divisional Round, then lost to New England 7-10 in the AFC Championship in a game that could have gone either way.

The bold bet: Jaylen Waddle. Rather than stand pat, the Broncos traded their 1st, 3rd, and 4th round picks to acquire the elite receiver, called the "most impactful trade of the offseason" by multiple analysts.
Waddle's credentials are impeccable. In 2025, he had 64 receptions for 910 yards and 6 TDs on 100 targets — a proven No. 1 receiver at the peak of his powers.
The downside: No draft capital. First pick at #62 after trading away early rounds; all-in gamble on adding proven talent over future uncertainty.

left.title: Trades & Major Transactions
items: TradeJaylen Waddle, WR acquired for 1st, 3rd, & 4th round picks — the boldest move of Denver's offseason, adding an elite receiving talent to a contending roster.
SignedSupporting Waddle with defensive depth signings to maintain the AFC Championship defense that was strong through the playoff run.
DraftDT Tyler Onyedim at #62 (first available pick) — fits Vance Joseph's one-gap defensive scheme.
Injury concernBo Nix suffered injuries in playoff losses; his health going into camp is critical to the Super Bowl equation.
RetainedDefensive core and offensive weapons kept together to maintain continuity in a Super Bowl push.

right.title: Player Updates & Camp Battles
items: Bo Nix, QB. The rookie sensation had a strong 2025 but suffered injuries in the playoff losses; his health status entering camp is the single biggest variable in a Super Bowl trajectory.
Jaylen Waddle, WR. The acquisition signal: Denver believes it's ready to win now. Waddle's integration with Nix and the offensive scheme will dominate offensive film study this August.
The chemistry question. A rookie QB with a new No. 1 receiver creates timing and chemistry work; Waddle is proven but hasn't played with Nix.
Vance Joseph's defense. The defensive coordinator's unit was strong through the AFC Championship loss; it returns as the roster's established strength.
Tyler Onyedim, DT. The one draft pick represents a one-gap scheme fit rather than a BPA approach; scheme continuity is the priority.

right.title: The Bottom Line
items: Denver went all-in by trading 1st, 3rd, and 4th round picks for Jaylen Waddle, betting that proven elite talent beats draft uncertainty on a Super Bowl contender. Bo Nix's health is the pivot point — if the rookie QB is fully recovered, Nix-to-Waddle becomes one of the most potent QB-to-receiver combinations in football. If there are lingering issues from the playoff injuries, the trade's value becomes questionable. This camp will show whether the Waddle gamble was genius or premature. Vance Joseph's defense remains the most reliable unit; if it delivers again, and if Nix is healthy, Denver has a legitimate Super Bowl pathway.

teams.sources: ESPN (2026 Broncos training camp & offseason coverage) · NFL.com · Broncos.com · Denver Post · Sports Illustrated / Broncos Blitz · FOX31 Denver.

teams.name: Lions
teams.subhead: 2026 training camp edition — a retooled offensive line, a new offensive coordinator and one central question hanging over Allen Park: has the Super Bowl window closed?

left.title: Front Office & Leadership
items: New offensive coordinator. Detroit hired Drew Petzing to run the offense — the latest coordinator turnover of the Dan Campbell era, and the most consequential given how far the 2025 season fell short of expectations.
Campbell and Holmes both back. The head coach/GM pairing survived a disappointing 2025 intact, but the roster around them was reshaped aggressively rather than preserved.

Holmes' stated approach: re-sign the players he already knows fit the culture — CB Rock Ya-Sin and LB Malcolm Rodriguez headlined that group — then fill gaps with mid-tier veterans rather than top-of-market strikes.

left.title: Trades & Major Transactions
items: TradeDavid Montgomery to Houston. The veteran back who formed half of Detroit's signature committee was dealt to the Texans, ending the Montgomery–Gibbs pairing.
ReleasedTaylor Decker and Graham Glasgow both cut loose as Detroit tore down and rebuilt an offensive line that had been the team's identity.
SignedIsiah Pacheco, RB — the splashiest addition of the offseason and Montgomery's direct replacement. Two-time Super Bowl champion in Kansas City, but coming off two injury-impacted seasons.
SignedC Cade Mays, T Larry Borom and G Ben Bartch — the offensive line reset in three moves.
SignedTE Tyler Conklin, CB Roger McCreary, DB Christian Izien, S Chuck Clark, CB Avonte Maddox, QB Teddy Bridgewater, EDGE D.J. Wonnum (1 yr, up to $6M).
Re-signedCB Rock Ya-Sin and LB Malcolm Rodriguez.
LostNT DJ Reader to the New York Giants; QB Kyle Allen to Buffalo (2 yr / $6.1M).

left.title: Rumor Mill
items: Speculation"Has the window closed?" is the framing national outlets have attached to this camp. From 2023–25 Detroit opened every season as a legitimate contender; 2025 ended well short, and the offseason churn read as a response to that.
SpeculationThe safety room is the quiet worry — a tandem that powered the 2023 run now carries real availability questions into a season Detroit can't afford to waste.

right.title: Player Updates & Camp Battles
items: Penei Sewell, OT. Voted the NFL's No. 1 offensive tackle in an ESPN poll of executives, coaches and scouts — and now moving from right tackle to left, the single biggest technical adjustment on the roster.
Jared Goff, QB. Back under a new coordinator in Petzing. The core he throws to is intact, which is why Detroit's offense still projects as one of the league's most explosive.
Jahmyr Gibbs, RB. No longer splitting with Montgomery. How much of that vacated workload he absorbs — versus Pacheco — is the offense's defining camp question.
Amon-Ra St. Brown & Jameson Williams, WR. Both return, giving Goff continuity at receiver even as the line and backfield turn over.
Isiah Pacheco, RB. Health is the whole story. Two injury-shortened seasons in Kansas City preceded this deal.
Offensive line, rebuilt. With Decker and Glasgow gone and Sewell sliding left, Detroit is auditioning a substantially new five-man front in camp.
Safety tandem. Both starters carry serious availability concerns into 2026 — a unit that was a strength is now a question.

right.title: Latest Roster Moves

Signed with the New York Giants

right.title: The Bottom Line
items: Detroit answered a disappointing 2025 by changing everything except the people in charge: new coordinator, new line, new backfield partner, same Campbell and Holmes. The skill core — Goff, Gibbs, St. Brown, Williams — is good enough to carry an explosive offense, but it now sits behind a front five that has to be assembled in real time, with Sewell learning left tackle on the fly. If the line settles early, the window is still open. If it doesn't, this becomes the season the national narrative already wrote.

teams.name: Packers
teams.subhead: 2026 training camp edition — two torn ACLs headline camp, and the roster around Jordan Love may be the best in the NFC once they heal.

left.title: Front Office & Leadership
items: Continuity at the top. Matt LaFleur and GM Brian Gutekunst both return, and Gutekunst spent the offseason patching the two units that failed Green Bay in 2025: the interior defensive line and the offensive line.
Gutekunst on the rehabs: Tucker Kraft is slightly ahead of schedule and Micah Parsons is progressing quickly — the GM's own framing heading into camp.
Roster math. With Parsons expected to open on PUP, Green Bay gets a free 53-man spot early — a dilemma insiders have flagged as a real edge in a deep front seven.

left.title: Trades & Major Transactions
items: TradeZaire Franklin, LB acquired to replace Quay Walker, who left in free agency — a direct swap of tackling production at a position of need.
SignedJavon Hargrave, DT — the veteran presence Green Bay wanted on a defensive front that could not stop the run.
Re-signedWR Bo Melton and G Donovan Jennings in April.
DraftDT Chris McClellan in the third round — more interior help. Five draft picks and 10 rookie free agents signed May 1.
LostLB Quay Walker departed in free agency.

left.title: Rumor Mill
items: SpeculationNational projections have Green Bay as a top-tier NFC roster the moment Parsons and Kraft are back — which is also the argument that the season turns entirely on Jordan Love's play in the meantime.
SpeculationRotational defensive linemen are the roster bubble to watch; run defense was the stated reason the depth chart changed.

right.title: Player Updates & Camp Battles
items: Micah Parsons, EDGE. Torn ACL against Denver. LaFleur said he'd begin camp on PUP, and Parsons himself expects to miss the first three or four games.
Tucker Kraft, TE. Torn ACL in Week 9 vs. Carolina. Kraft insists he'll play Week 1 with no restricted workload — and the front office says he's ahead of schedule.

Zach Tom, RT. The Packers call him their best offensive lineman. He played through injuries, shut it down for the final four games, had knee surgery to repair a partially torn patellar tendon, and did not practice this spring. His return is the key to settling a line that struggled.
Jordan Love, QB. Underlying numbers point to a monster season if the supporting cast holds — the roster is built for it.
Javon Hargrave, DT. Signed to fix a run defense that leaked all season; pairs with rookie Chris McClellan inside.
Bubble watch. Several rotational defensive linemen must perform in camp to keep roster spots after the depth-chart shakeup.

right.title: Latest Roster Moves

Expected to open training camp on PUP

right.title: The Bottom Line
items: Green Bay's 2026 is a health story before it's anything else. The roster — with Parsons and Kraft back — is arguably the NFC's deepest, but Parsons has already put a three-to-four-game absence on the record and Zach Tom hasn't practiced since knee surgery. The front office response was targeted rather than splashy: Franklin for Walker, Hargrave and a third-round tackle for a run defense that couldn't hold up. Survive September, and the back half of this schedule looks very different.

teams.name: Texans
teams.subhead: 2026 training camp edition — a divisional-round exit, a rebuilt offensive line for the second straight year, and a franchise quarterback still waiting on an extension.

left.title: Front Office & Leadership
items: The Stroud contract is the story. Houston picked up C.J. Stroud's fifth-year option but there have been no extension talks. Stroud's own framing this spring: "I've held up my bargain."
Offensive line, rebuilt again. For the second consecutive offseason, Houston reworked the line — and drew criticism for how it went about it in the draft.
The offensive identity shift: the front office wants a punishing run game to make Houston a better red-zone and play-action team, which is exactly why it went and got a veteran back.

left.title: Trades & Major Transactions
items: TradeDavid Montgomery, RB acquired from Detroit, then signed to a two-year, $16.5M extension — the centerpiece of the new run-first plan.
SignedTE Foster Moreau, filling in after starter Dalton Schultz was lost to injury during the postseason.
TradeAcquired P Kai Kroeger and a 2028 seventh from New Orleans for a 2029 sixth.
Line workMultiple offensive line additions across free agency and the draft — the position group Houston has now spent two straight offseasons trying to fix.

left.title: Rumor Mill
items: SpeculationWith no extension signed, national outlets have run hypothetical C.J. Stroud trade pitches and published estimates of his trade value. These are analyst exercises, not reported conversations — but they exist because the contract doesn't.

right.title: Player Updates & Camp Battles
items: C.J. Stroud, QB. Nobody in camp will be under a brighter spotlight. He is noticeably leaner and more mobile after a stricter diet and training regimen, and has posted faster conditioning times. One person around the team called it the best offseason he's had.
How he's handled it matters. Stroud has responded to the contract limbo by looking sharp rather than sulking — the Texans have gone out of their way to say so publicly.
David Montgomery, RB. Brought in to change what Houston's offense is: heavier, more physical, better inside the 20.
Dalton Schultz, TE. The postseason injury that cost Houston its starter is why Foster Moreau is here.
The offensive line. Two years of investment, and it still has to prove it can protect the franchise quarterback the club hasn't paid yet.
DeMeco Ryans' defense carried Houston to a divisional round; it returns as the roster's most reliable unit.

right.title: Latest Roster Moves

Fifth-year option exercised; no extension talks

right.title: The Bottom Line
items: Houston is a good team with one unresolved sentence in its future. The defense is legitimate, the run game just got heavier, and the offensive line has absorbed two offseasons of resources. But C.J. Stroud is playing on a fifth-year option with no extension conversation happening, and the longer that lasts, the louder the hypotheticals get. To his credit, he showed up in the best shape of his career. The Texans have every incentive to make this a non-story by September.

teams.name: Colts
teams.subhead: 2026 training camp edition — $88M says Daniel Jones is the starter, three key players are rehabbing surgeries, and Anthony Richardson is back in the building.

left.title: Front Office & Leadership
items: The Colts committed to Daniel Jones on a two-year, $88M deal — an emphatic answer to a quarterback question that has followed this franchise for years.

Anthony Richardson Sr. returned. He requested a trade earlier in the offseason, then came back during the voluntary program and drew praise from coaches and teammates for his professionalism and mentality.
Last year's bill is still being paid. Indianapolis traded two first-round picks for CB Sauce Gardner — the kind of move that removes any patience from the timeline.
The pass rush was allowed to leave. Kwity Paye and Samson Ebukam both walked in free agency, an unusual choice for a team otherwise pushing chips in.

left.title: Trades & Major Transactions
items: SignedDaniel Jones, QB — two years, $88M, back as the unambiguous starter.
SignedAlec Pierce, WR — four years, $114M on March 9, one of the largest receiver contracts of the offseason.
SignedEDGE Arden Key — the veteran expected to absorb some of the vacated pass-rush role.
SignedS Thomas from Dallas, joining a safety room that was thin behind Cam Bynum.
LostEDGE Kwity Paye and EDGE Samson Ebukam (to Atlanta) both departed in free agency.

right.title: Player Updates & Camp Battles
items: Daniel Jones, QB. Rehabbed an Achilles this offseason and is expected to be ready for the start of camp, operating the starting offense in team sessions from day one.
Alec Pierce, WR. Signed for $114M in March, then underwent a "clean-up procedure" on his left ankle. A candidate to open camp on PUP.
DeForest Buckner, DT. Rehabbing a neck issue and also a PUP candidate — the third influential Colt coming off surgery.
Anthony Richardson Sr., QB. Trade request behind him, back in the building, and by all accounts handling a backup role the right way. How the room shakes out behind Jones is a genuine camp question.
Riley Leonard, QB. The third name in a quarterback room the team's own preview treats as unsettled beyond QB1.
Arden Key, EDGE. Carrying more than a veteran signing usually does, given who left.

right.title: The Bottom Line
items: Indianapolis has spent aggressively in every direction — two first-round picks for Sauce Gardner, $88M for Daniel Jones, $114M for Alec Pierce — and now waits to see who is healthy enough to use it. Jones (Achilles), Pierce (ankle) and Buckner (neck) all spent the offseason rehabbing, with two of them PUP candidates. Meanwhile the edge rush walked out the door. It is a roster with a very high ceiling and an unusually large number of medical asterisks.

teams.name: Jaguars
teams.subhead: 2026 training camp edition — defending AFC South champions return intact, Liam Coen's second year, and the challenge of repeating in a competitive division.

left.title: Front Office & Leadership
items: Continuity is the strategy. Jacksonville won the AFC South at 13–4 with Liam Coen in his first year, then lost a Wild Card game to Buffalo 27–24 that could easily have gone the other way.
Minimal roster moves. Rather than overhaul, the Jaguars took a conservative approach in free agency with only limited external signings, trusting the foundation already in place.
Trevor Lawrence secured long-term. The quarterback is locked in on a five-year, $275M deal with $200M guaranteed, giving the franchise continuity at the most important position.
The narrative going forward: Can a young core built by Coen repeat their success in a competitive AFC South?

left.title: Trades & Major Transactions
items: TradeTravis Hunter, TE acquired (trade details TBD) — depth at tight end to support Lawrence.
SignedRB Chris Rodriguez Jr. — the lone significant external free agent addition.
DraftLimited by previous Travis Hunter trade capital, selected Nate Boerkircher, TE at #56 in the second round — a depth move criticized as early.
RetainedCore roster kept together with minimal departures, maintaining the chemistry that led to division championship.

right.title: Player Updates & Camp Battles
items: Trevor Lawrence, QB. Playing on an $88M annual average deal and operating as an MVP candidate entering Year 4. The continuity in system and staff under Coen should accelerate development.
The defense that won it. Jacksonville's defense was the backbone of their AFC South title run and returns largely intact, a major advantage in the repeat bid.
Chris Rodriguez Jr., RB. Added as a free agent, tasked with providing depth in the backfield alongside the established rotation.
Nate Boerkircher, TE. Second-round pick competing for depth snaps behind established tight ends.
Coen's system maturity. Year 2 of a head coach's system typically sees marked improvement; expectations are accordingly high.

right.title: The Bottom Line
items: Jacksonville built something real in 2025 and trusted it enough to stay conservative in the offseason. Trevor Lawrence is locked in on a massive deal, the defense returns intact, and Liam Coen gets Year 2 to refine his system. The challenge is repeating in the AFC South while facing a potential Super Bowl rematch with Buffalo. This is a team banking on continuity over overhaul.

teams.sources: ESPN (2026 Jaguars training camp & offseason coverage) · NFL.com · Jaguars.com · Sports Illustrated / Jaguars Nation.

teams.name: Chiefs
teams.subhead: 2026 training camp edition — Patrick Mahomes' ACL recovery, a defensive youth injection, and the end of an era of playoff dominance.

left.title: Front Office & Leadership
items: A humbling 6-11. Kansas City missed the playoffs for the first time since 2014, ending an era of sustained excellence and raising questions about what's broken when an MVP candidate gets injured.

Mahomes' recovery is front and center. Patrick Mahomes suffered a torn ACL in Week 15 of 2025 and is reporting he feels stronger going into camp, though he's wearing a brace and compression sleeve for protection.
Defensive investment is urgent. The Chiefs drafted defensively with four of their first four picks, signaling a conviction that the defense is the immediate problem to solve.
The narrative: Can Mahomes' return and defensive youth reverse the slide before it becomes a pattern?

left.title: Trades & Major Transactions
items: SignedKenneth Walker III, RB — Super Bowl MVP running back, three-year deal worth $43.05M, bringing championship pedigree to the backfield.
DraftMansoor Delane, CB at #6 overall (traded up) — the team's cornerstone defensive back for the next decade.
DraftPeter Woods, DT at #29, part of the youth defensive overhaul focused on stopping the run.
RetainedL'Jarius Sneed, CB re-signed to anchor the secondary alongside Delane.
Program overhaulBrought back rookie head-start program; early camp returns showing promise in player development.

right.title: Player Updates & Camp Battles
items: Patrick Mahomes, QB. Recovering from a torn ACL suffered Week 15, reports feeling stronger than expected going into camp. The confidence is there, but the brace tells the real story of caution and recovery.

Mahomes' availability is the story. If he's truly back to form, the Chiefs have a path to redemption. If there's even a hint of hesitation, the 6-11 season becomes less of an anomaly and more of a warning sign.
Kenneth Walker III, RB. The Super Bowl MVP arrives to stabilize the ground game and bring winning experience to a reeling locker room.
Mansoor Delane, CB. First-overall defensive pick, tasked with becoming the generational cornerback the franchise has lacked.
The defense must deliver. Four first-four picks on defense mean those players must contribute immediately, not years from now.

right.title: Latest Roster Moves
head: Move
Detail
items: Recovering from torn ACL; reports strong

right.title: The Bottom Line
items: Kansas City's 6-11 season was a shock after 11 consecutive playoff appearances, and the road back starts with Patrick Mahomes' recovery from an ACL injury. The quarterback insists he's healthy, and early camp returns suggest it's true. The Chiefs are betting that Kenneth Walker III's leadership and a youth defensive class built around Mansoor Delane can stabilize the ship before questions about dynasty decline get louder. Everything depends on Mahomes truly being back and the defensive rookies contributing immediately.

teams.sources: ESPN (2026 Chiefs training camp & offseason coverage) · NFL.com · Chiefs.com · KSHB (Kansas City local coverage) · Sports Illustrated / Chiefs Maven.

teams.name: Chargers
teams.subhead: 2026 training camp edition — Mike McDaniel arrives to fix a broken offensive line, Jim Harbaugh faces Year 2 pressure, and redemption begins now.

left.title: Front Office & Leadership
items: The protection nightmare cost them. Los Angeles won 11 games but allowed 60 sacks in 2025 — a catastrophic offensive line performance that overshadowed an 11-6 record and led to a 3-16 Wild Card loss to New England.
The loss exposed everything. In that playoff game, the Chargers managed only 159 passing yards, took 6 sacks, and fumbled once — a systematic failure on the offensive line that can't be ignored.
Mike McDaniel is the fix. Jim Harbaugh brought in the respected offensive coordinator to redesign the scheme and hopefully improve protection schemes and execution.
Harbaugh's seat gets warmer. Year 2 of the experiment; another playoff loss and questions about the hire will intensify.

left.title: Trades & Major Transactions
items: SignedTyler Biadasz, C — #1 priority for offensive line, addressing the center position that was a weakness in 2025.
SignedCole Strange, G — guard help to stabilize the interior line, pairing with Biadasz.
SignedTE Charlie Kolar — $24.3M/3yr for receiving depth and pass-catching support.
RetainedKhalil Mack kept on the defensive end to anchor the pass rush despite salary considerations.
Draft focusAdditional offensive line depth through the draft to complete the overhaul of the unit that gave up 60 sacks.

right.title: Player Updates & Camp Battles
items: The offensive line is ground zero. Tyler Biadasz, Cole Strange, and additional draft picks will be competing to fix a unit that embarrassed itself in the Wild Card game.
Justin Herbert, QB. A year after avoiding catastrophic injury, Herbert needs competent pass protection to operate. The 60 sacks tell the story of how poorly he was protected in 2025.
Mike McDaniel's scheme test. The offensive coordinator arrives to fix the protection issues; his first camp will show whether the problem was personnel, scheme, or both.
Khalil Mack, EDGE. Retained on the defense to keep pass rush consistent, though the offensive line overhaul is the clear priority.
Charlie Kolar, TE. Added as a pass-catching option to give Herbert more targets in a league where that's increasingly important.

right.title: The Bottom Line
items: Los Angeles allowed 60 sacks, lost a playoff game badly, and called in Mike McDaniel to fix the offense. Tyler Biadasz and Cole Strange address the center and guard spots, but the offensive line rebuild is a work in progress that will dominate this camp. Jim Harbaugh's second season is already proving to be a prove-it moment; the 3-16 playoff loss erased the 11-6 regular season from the narrative. If McDaniel's scheme and the new pieces don't immediately improve protection, questions about Harbaugh's long-term fit will grow loudly.

teams.sources: ESPN (2026 Chargers training camp & offseason coverage) · NFL.com · Chargers.com · San Diego Union-Tribune · Sports Illustrated / Chargers Maven.

teams.name: Rams
teams.subhead: 2026 training camp edition — two blockbuster trades, the reigning MVP and the reigning Defensive Player of the Year on one roster, and Super Bowl favorite odds to carry.

left.title: Front Office & Leadership
items: All-in, stated plainly. After losing the NFC Championship Game to Seattle, Los Angeles spent the offseason signing big in free agency and making two blockbuster trades. Nobody in the building is describing this as anything other than a championship push.
Kliff Kingsbury joins the staff from Washington, adding another offensive voice around McVay and the reigning MVP.
Stafford, extended — sort of. The Rams got a deal done, but the arrangement remains effectively year-to-year, buying rookie Ty Simpson time to develop behind a 38-year-old starter.
Camp: players reported July 25; practices run July 26 – Aug. 7 at Loyola Marymount.

left.title: Trades & Major Transactions
items: TradeMyles Garrett acquired in June — the reigning Defensive Player of the Year. The cost was steep: EDGE Jared Verse, a 25-year-old two-time Pro Bowler, plus multiple picks including a 2027 first-rounder.
TradeTrent McDuffie from Kansas City in March, then signed the All-Pro corner to a four-year, $120M extension. Called the biggest trade of the offseason before Garrett topped it.
SignedCB Jaylen Watson — Kansas City's other starting corner from last season, giving Los Angeles both halves of the Chiefs' 2025 secondary.
SignedLS Joe Cardona to a two-year deal, solidifying the specialist operation.
DraftQB Ty Simpson — the succession plan, still unsigned as camp opened.

left.title: Rumor Mill
items: SpeculationAaron Donald, un-retired? Trading for Garrett in June revived talk of a Donald return to play alongside the reigning DPOY. McVay said the team is "of course" open to it — and that the decision belongs entirely to Donald.
ContractPuka Nacua has a looming, potentially top-of-market extension ahead of him.

right.title: Player Updates & Camp Battles
items: Matthew Stafford, QB. Reigning MVP, entering his age-38 season. The recurring question is whether the Rams should again limit his camp workload — a real debate given how 2025 ended for him.
Myles Garrett, EDGE. Arrives as the best defensive player in football and the single biggest reason Los Angeles opened as a Super Bowl favorite.
Trent McDuffie, CB. $120M extension in hand, paired with former Chiefs teammate Jaylen Watson — a secondary rebuilt in one transaction cycle.
Puka Nacua, WR. Back after a stint in rehab and continuing that work, with a major extension on the horizon. Both matter to how 2026 goes.
Backup QB battle. Rookie Ty Simpson, still unsigned as camp opened, against Stetson Bennett for the job behind Stafford.
The hype problem. ESPN's framing of this camp is simply whether the Rams can live up to it — there is no version of 2026 where a conference title game is a satisfying result.

right.title: Latest Roster Moves
head: Move
Detail
items: Acquired by trade in June — reigning DPOY

right.title: The Bottom Line
items: Los Angeles lost a conference championship game and responded by acquiring the reigning Defensive Player of the Year, both of Kansas City's starting corners, and an extension for the MVP who is about to turn 38. There is no hedge in this roster and no patience built into it. The window is this year, McVay knows it, and the only questions left are Stafford's workload, Nacua's extension, and whether Aaron Donald picks up the phone.
