teams.name: Raiders
teams.subhead: 2026 training camp edition — a unique redshirt-Heisman model, Fernando Mendoza learning behind Kirk Cousins, and Klint Kubiak's Super Bowl OC pedigree.

left.title: Front Office & Leadership
items: Unprecedented quarterback strategy. Las Vegas drafted Heisman winner Fernando Mendoza #1 overall with the express plan to have him sit behind Kirk Cousins in a redshirt-rookie model designed to develop rather than rush the prospect.

Kubiak brings championship pedigree. Hired Super Bowl offensive coordinator Klint Kubiak (ex-Denver OC) as head coach, signaling ambition to build a contender with veteran leadership and experienced coaching.
Aggressive free agency. The Raiders spent over $280M in free agency, building a veteran roster with the intention of competing immediately while Mendoza develops.
The bet: patience with a prize. Most teams can't afford to sit a #1 pick; Las Vegas is betting that developing Mendoza slowly creates a generational advantage when he takes over.

left.title: Trades & Major Transactions
items: SignedKirk Cousins, QB — $20M/1yr guaranteed, brought in as both starting QB and mentor to Ferdinand Mendoza in an unprecedented arrangement.
DraftedFernando Mendoza, QB #1 overall — Heisman winner, 41 TDs, 6 INTs, 72% completion, 3,535 yards, National Champion, Consensus All-American — sitting Year 1.
SignedTyler Linderbaum, C — highest-paid center in football, anchoring the offensive line for Kirk Cousins' operation.
SignedLBs Nakobe Dean and Quay Walker — elite defensive additions to complement a veteran pass rush and coverage group.
Coaching staff overhaulKubiak brings a proven Super Bowl offensive system to the franchise, creating continuity for Cousins and Mendoza.

right.title: Player Updates & Camp Battles
items: Kirk Cousins, QB. Playing mentor to the future franchise QB while leading a veteran roster in 2026. His on-field teaching and locker-room presence will directly impact Mendoza's development.

Fernando Mendoza, QB (sitting Year 1). The Heisman winner is in a unique situation: learn the pro game, study Cousins, develop timing with receivers, and take over a veteran-ready roster in 2027 — not immediately thrust into starting before he's ready.
Tyler Linderbaum, C. The highest-paid center in football, tasked with stabilizing the line for both Cousins and the eventual Mendoza transition.
Nakobe Dean & Quay Walker, LBs. Elite defensive acquisitions adding immediate impact to a unit being built around veteran leadership.
The offensive philosophy. Klint Kubiak's Super Bowl system arrives intact; Cousins knows it, and Mendoza will learn it during Year 1 of sitdown.

right.title: Latest Roster Moves
head: Move
Detail
items: Super Bowl OC hired as coach

right.title: The Bottom Line
items: Las Vegas has implemented an unprecedented strategy: draft a Heisman winner #1 overall, sit him for a year, and develop him behind a Super Bowl offensive coordinator and veteran quarterback. Fernando Mendoza's credentials are impeccable (41 TDs, 6 INTs, National Champion), but the redshirt approach risks losing a year of elite rookie receiver production and salary cap flexibility. If Mendoza truly thrives after a year of patient development, Las Vegas will have built something generational. If the strategy doesn't work, questions about the #1 overall decision will linger. For now, Kirk Cousins runs the offense, Klint Kubiak's system gets implemented, and Mendoza watches from the sideline — a camp storyline unlike any other in football.

teams.sources: ESPN (2026 Raiders training camp & offseason coverage) · NFL.com · Raiders.com · Las Vegas Review-Journal · Sports Illustrated / Raiders Maven.

teams.name: Dolphins
teams.subhead: 2026 training camp edition — Tua is gone, Waddle is gone, Jeff Hafley is in, and a $67.5M quarterback from Green Bay inherits one of the league's thinnest receiver rooms.

left.title: Front Office & Leadership
items: Jeff Hafley takes over a roster in the middle of near-total turnover — and brought Green Bay's offensive structure with him, including coordinator Sullivan and the quarterback.
The Tua era ended abruptly. Miami cut Tua Tagovailoa, who signed with Atlanta, and traded Jaylen Waddle. Both moves left the roster, in the words of one national preview, severely talent deficient.
The honest framing: previews of this camp are titled some version of brace for growing pains. Nobody inside or outside the building is selling 2026 as a contention year.
The plan is the draft class — two first-rounders and four more picks expected to play immediately.

left.title: Trades & Major Transactions
items: SignedMalik Willis, QB — three years, $67.5M, following Hafley and Sullivan from Green Bay. In 11 appearances behind Jordan Love he completed 79% of his passes at 10.9 yards per attempt with six touchdowns and zero interceptions.
ReleasedTua Tagovailoa, QB — signed with Atlanta, where he now competes for that job.
TradeJaylen Waddle, WR dealt away, gutting the receiver room in the same offseason.
DraftOT Kadyn Proctor (1st), CB Chris Johnson (1st), LB Jacob Rodriguez (2nd), WR Chris Bell (3rd), EDGE Trey Moore (4th), LB Kyle Loui (4th).
SignedEDGE Joshua Uche (from Philadelphia) and EDGE David Ojabo; WR Jalen Tolbert added from Dallas.

right.title: Player Updates & Camp Battles
items: Malik Willis, QB. Enters camp as the clear-cut projected starter. His Green Bay efficiency numbers are excellent and came in a very small, very protected sample — that gap is the season's central question.
Quinn Ewers, QB. The only other quarterback on the roster with NFL experience: three rookie starts, 83 attempts, 66% completions, 7.5 yards per attempt, three touchdowns and three interceptions.
De'Von Achane, RB. The offense's one unambiguous strength — 1,350 rushing yards and eight touchdowns in 2025. Expect the run game to carry a first-year starter.
The receiver room is the problem. Chris Bell, TuTu Atwell, Jalen Tolbert and Malik Washington is, by most national assessments, among the weakest groups in the league.
Kadyn Proctor, OT & Chris Johnson, CB. Two first-round rookies expected to start on a roster with no one blocking their path.
Uche & Ojabo, EDGE. Low-cost bets on former high-pedigree rushers looking to restart their careers.

right.title: Latest Roster Moves
head: Move
Detail
items: 3 yr / $67.5M, followed Hafley from Green Bay

right.title: The Bottom Line
items: Miami removed its quarterback and its second receiver in the same offseason and replaced them with a coach's familiar backup and two first-round rookies. That is not a retool, it is a teardown with a plausible story attached: Willis was genuinely excellent in limited Green Bay work, Achane can carry an offense, and six early picks will play right away. The receiver room says growing pains. Everyone in South Florida already knows it.

teams.sources: ESPN (2026 Dolphins training camp preview) · MiamiDolphins.com camp previews · Yahoo Sports · WalterFootball · Sports Illustrated / Dolphins OnSI · Dolphin Seer.

teams.name: Vikings
teams.subhead: 2026 training camp edition — no general manager, an open quarterback competition, and a head coach who has quietly become the most powerful person in the building.

left.title: Front Office & Leadership
items: GM fired. Minnesota dismissed Kwesi Adofo-Mensah and deliberately did not name a replacement before the draft. Longtime executive Rob Brzezinski took over day-to-day football operations in the interim.

O'Connell's power grows. The 2024 Coach of the Year already drove personnel alongside Adofo-Mensah; league sources expect he ends up with more formal authority even if it never appears in contract language. Functionally, everything now starts with him.

RumorReporting since the firing has hinted at friction and "imperfect power dynamics" between coach and GM. O'Connell has pushed back publicly, calling the relationship strong and any suggestion otherwise "not accurate in any way, shape, or form."
Brian Flores returns as defensive coordinator — the one piece of the operation nobody questioned.

left.title: Trades & Major Transactions
items: SignedKyler Murray, QB — the former No. 1 overall pick on a one-year deal at the veteran minimum, with Arizona paying the remainder of his $36.5M guarantee for 2026. One of the most lopsided cost structures in the league.
Re-signedQB Carson Wentz, filling out a room of McCarthy, Murray and Wentz.
SignedT Ryan Van Demark via offer sheet — Buffalo declined to match. LB Eric Wilson on a multiyear deal after one of his best seasons since 2020.
SignedCB Pierre from Pittsburgh, who overlapped with Flores there — a scheme-fit add to the corner room.
SignedP Johnny Hekker (1 yr), completing an all-Pro-credentialed specialist trio with K Will Reichard and LS Andrew DePaola.
LostP Ryan Wright to New Orleans on a four-year deal after four seasons in Minnesota.

right.title: Player Updates & Camp Battles
items: QB1 is genuinely open. O'Connell declared an open competition between Kyler Murray and J.J. McCarthy. Murray is the heavy favorite — a steadier option after a season in which McCarthy was handed the job having never taken a regular-season NFL snap.
Rookie DL Banks (Florida), 1st round. Recovering from a foot injury, but O'Connell has publicly backed his ability to get on the field.
Harrison Smith, S. Unless he chooses to play rather than retire, Minnesota has an opening at safety for the first time in 15 seasons.
Center, wide open. Ryan Kelly's retirement leaves the job to utility lineman Blake Brandel, who started nine games there in 2025 and gets the first look.

Christian Darrisaw, LT. Started just 10 games last season after a knee injury — part of an offensive line battered all year. Kelly landed in concussion protocol three separate times and played only eight games.
Specialists are a strength. Hekker, Reichard and DePaola give Minnesota arguably the league's best kicking operation.

right.title: Camp Calendar
items: First real look at Murray vs. McCarthy under live conditions
Banks' foot, Brandel at center, Smith's retirement decision

right.title: The Bottom Line
items: Minnesota is running a season without a permanent general manager, with a quarterback room that includes the man they drafted in the first round, a former No. 1 overall pick playing for the minimum, and a veteran third. That is either flexibility or instability depending on how August goes. Kevin O'Connell owns all of it now — the roster, the call on McCarthy, and the outcome. Flores' defense buys margin; the offensive line's health decides how much.

teams.sources: ESPN (Vikings camp preview & free agency tracker) · Vikings.com position previews · NFL.com · Daily Norseman · Bleacher Report · Pro Football Rumors · KARE 11 · Sports Illustrated.

teams.name: Patriots
teams.subhead: 2026 training camp edition — defending AFC champions, A.J. Brown in the building, and one starter whose attendance is still an open question.

left.title: Front Office & Leadership
items: From worst to the Super Bowl. New England went 14–3, beat the Chargers and Texans, took the AFC Championship from Denver 10–7, and lost Super Bowl LX to Seattle 29–13.
The stated goal for camp: "weaponize Drake's mind" as Maye enters his second season in Josh McDaniels' system — less installation, more autonomy.
The front office spent like a contender, adding a receiver in free agency and then paying a first-round pick for a second one in June.
Reality checkESPN's Football Power Index does not rank the defending AFC champions as the best team in their own division — Buffalo is ahead of them, and New England sits seventh in the conference.

left.title: Trades & Major Transactions
items: TradeA.J. Brown from Philadelphia, completed in June, for a first- and a fifth-round pick. From 2022–25 no receiver in football commanded a larger share of his team's receiving yards.
SignedWR Romeo Doubs — the big-ticket offensive acquisition before Brown, giving Maye two new outside targets.
SignedFurther offensive line investment, the quieter priority of the offseason and the one that keeps Maye upright.
AddedTE Eli Raridon — another pass-catching option in a room that needed one.
Chemistry started early: Brown wasted no time working with Maye at minicamp.

right.title: Player Updates & Camp Battles
items: Drake Maye, QB. Led New England to a Super Bowl and finished second in MVP voting. With Brown and Doubs added, the coaching staff believes he can be more dangerous in Year 2 of McDaniels' offense.
AttendanceChristian Gonzalez, CB. Whether the star corner is at camp at all is the question ESPN built its entire Patriots preview around — the single biggest unresolved item in the building.
A.J. Brown, WR. Cost a first-rounder and immediately became the offense's focal point. Already building timing with Maye.
Romeo Doubs, WR. Signed before Brown; now the complement rather than the centerpiece, which is a better job for him.
Gabe Jacas is among the young defenders local coverage has flagged as a player to watch through August.
Camp runs through Aug. 20 at Gillette Stadium.

right.title: Latest Roster Moves
head: Move
Detail
items: Trade with Philadelphia for a first and a fifth
Sent to Philadelphia in the Brown deal

right.title: The Bottom Line
items: New England got to a Super Bowl a year early and then behaved like a team that intends to go back: it bought the best available receiver with first-round capital and put him next to the MVP runner-up. The counterweight is that the models don't buy it — the Bills rank ahead of them, and Denver and Seattle both look the same as they did in January. The one thing that could unravel a very good summer is Christian Gonzalez's attendance, which is still unresolved as camp opens.

teams.sources: ESPN (2026 Patriots training camp preview; Football Power Index) · NFL.com · NBC Sports Boston · 98.5 The Sports Hub · Sports Illustrated / Patriots Country · Heavy.com · Wikipedia (2025 Patriots season).

teams.name: Saints
teams.subhead: 2026 training camp edition — Tyler Shough is the unquestioned starter, the weapons around him are all new, and Kellen Moore's offense is about to look different.

left.title: Front Office & Leadership
items: Year 2 of Kellen Moore. The Saints closed 2025 winning four of their final five with Shough under center — enough to convert a rebuild into something that looks like a plan.

The offense is being rebuilt on purpose. Moore is layering in more under-center runs and multi-tight-end sets on top of his existing motion-and-balance principles. Expect it to look meaningfully different from 2025 tape.
Protect the young quarterback. That was the stated logic behind the biggest contract of the offseason, and it drove the offseason's priority list from the first day of free agency.
Open questionsThe futures of Taysom Hill and long-time DE Cameron Jordan remain among the last unresolved items on the roster.

left.title: Trades & Major Transactions
items: SignedDavid Edwards, G (from Buffalo) — four years with $45M guaranteed and a $20M signing bonus. The offensive line investment the front office said Shough needed.
SignedRB Travis Etienne Jr., TE Noah Fant and LB Kaden Elliss — three starters added in one wave.
SignedP Ryan Wright (ex-Vikings) — four years, $8M guaranteed, closing one of the roster's genuine holes.
TradeAcquired EDGE Tyree Wilson from Las Vegas during the draft, swapping pick No. 150 for Wilson and pick No. 219.
TradeSent P Kai Kroeger and a 2028 seventh to Houston for a 2029 sixth.
Re-signedQB Hunter Dekkers, 25, with no guaranteed money after an injury-hit UFL season.

right.title: Player Updates & Camp Battles
items: Tyler Shough, QB. The 2025 second-rounder took over mid-season and justified the pick, closing the year 4–1. He opens his second camp as the unquestioned offensive leader — no competition, no hedge.
Chris Olave & Jordyn Tyson, WR. The high-flying tandem Moore now builds around. Tyson's arrival changes the geometry of the passing game.

The backfield split. Travis Etienne Jr. cleared 1,000 yards in three of four seasons in Jacksonville. How his workload divides with franchise all-time leading rusher Alvin Kamara is the season's most interesting subplot.
Noah Fant, TE. Fits directly into the multi-tight-end packages Moore is adding.
David Edwards, G. Anchors an interior that has to hold up for a quarterback still in his first full year as a starter.
Tyree Wilson, EDGE. A low-cost draft-weekend swing on a former top-10 pick who needed a change of scenery.

right.title: Latest Roster Moves
head: Move
Detail
items: Trade with Las Vegas on draft weekend
Traded to Houston with a 2028 seventh

right.title: The Bottom Line
items: New Orleans spent this offseason doing the unglamorous thing: it bought a guard, a punter, a running back and a tight end, and told everyone the quarterback job belongs to Tyler Shough with no asterisk. That is what conviction looks like from a front office that had none of it a year ago. Moore's offense will run heavier and more under center; Etienne and Kamara will split a backfield; Olave and Tyson give the whole thing a ceiling. The rebuild is no longer theoretical.

teams.sources: ESPN (2026 Saints training camp preview & free agency tracker) · NewOrleansSaints.com · NFL.com · Canal Street Chronicles · Louisiana Sports.

teams.name: Giants
teams.subhead: 2026 training camp edition — John Harbaugh takes over, nearly every skill player around Jaxson Dart is new, and expectations have moved for the first time in years.

left.title: Front Office & Leadership
items: Harbaugh hired. Fired by Baltimore after 18 seasons, John Harbaugh, 63, agreed to a five-year contract and was introduced as head coach in January. Ownership wanted a proven winner who runs a tight ship; they got the coach who won Super Bowl XLVII.
Full staff named. Matt Nagy runs the offense, Dennard Wilson the defense, and Chris Horton special teams while also serving as assistant head coach.
Nagy's fingerprint: heavy multiple-tight-end usage, the same structure he leaned on in Kansas City and Chicago — which explains where the money went in March.
The mandate has changed. Between a Super Bowl-winning coach and a second-year quarterback, this is the first Giants camp in years opening with real expectations attached.

left.title: Trades & Major Transactions
items: SignedIsaiah Likely, TE — three years, $40M, following Harbaugh from Baltimore. Widely graded one of the best value moves of the offseason and the centerpiece of Nagy's two-TE plan.
SignedWR Darnell Mooney and WR Calvin Austin III earlier in free agency; WR Isaiah Hodgins re-signed. Six receivers added in total.
TradeDexter Lawrence II to Cincinnati for the No. 10 overall pick — a straight one-for-one swap of a three-time Pro Bowl nose tackle for premium draft capital.
SignedDT DJ Reader (from Detroit) and DT Shelby Harris — the interior rebuilt after Lawrence's exit.
SignedS Ar'Darius Washington, plus Edmunds, Newsome, Reese and Hood across the front seven and secondary.
LostThe team's leading slot target departed for $78M elsewhere — the one significant subtraction from an otherwise additive offseason.

right.title: Player Updates & Camp Battles
items: Jaxson Dart, QB. Threw for 15 touchdowns and ran for nine more in 12 rookie starts. He is the undisputed starter, but told ESPN this spring it feels like last year all over again — learning a new offense for the second straight season. His development is the franchise's whole 2026.
Jameis Winston, QB2. Described internally as a premium, stabilizing insurance policy — a real backup rather than a competition.
Isaiah Likely, TE. Arrives knowing Harbaugh's standard and steps into a scheme designed to feature the position.
Receiver room, rebuilt from scratch. Mooney, Austin III and four more additions mean Dart is throwing to an almost entirely different group than he did as a rookie.
Interior defensive line. Reader and Harris give New York the run-stuffing weight it lacked; combined with Edmunds and Newsome, the defense should simply be more competitive.
Continuity is the risk. New coach, new coordinator, new pass catchers — installation speed is the story of this camp.

right.title: Latest Roster Moves
head: Move
Detail
items: Hired as head coach, five-year deal

right.title: The Bottom Line
items: New York did the two things a rebuilding team almost never gets to do in the same offseason: hire a coach with a Super Bowl ring and eighteen years of institutional credibility, and hand him a young quarterback who already flashed. Then it spent, replacing nearly every skill player around Jaxson Dart and finally putting weight on the interior defensive line. The catch is that Dart is learning his second offense in two years. If Nagy's install lands by September, this is the most improved roster in the division.

teams.sources: Giants.com (coaching staff, free agency tracker) · ESPN (2026 Giants training camp preview) · NFL.com · NBC Sports · Associated Press · Newsweek · Big Blue View · ClutchPoints.

teams.name: Jets
teams.subhead: 2026 training camp edition — half the staff replaced, three first-round picks, Geno Smith back in green, and a head coach who probably needs results now.

left.title: Front Office & Leadership
items: Hot seatAaron Glenn's make-or-break year. He replaced half his coaching staff — including both coordinators — rebuilt the defense, and imported a veteran quarterback to stabilize a position that has changed hands almost annually.
GM Darren Mougey's brief was depth and competition, and the draft reflected it: three first-round picks used on three different position groups.
The honest assessment from national previews: this collection of players is unlikely to produce immediate results, and expectations remain modest.

left.title: Trades & Major Transactions
items: TradeJustin Fields to Kansas City — ushered out after a disappointing 2025, closing another short quarterback chapter.
SignedQB Geno Smith, back in New York after a season with the Raiders, plus QB Bailey Zappe.
DraftThree first-rounders: EDGE David Bailey, TE Kenyon Sadiq and WR Omar Cooper Jr., then CB D'Angelo Ponds (2nd) and QB Cade Klubnik (4th).
SignedCB Nahshon Wright, EDGE Joseph Ossai and EDGE Kingsley Enagbare — the rebuilt defensive rotation.

right.title: Player Updates & Camp Battles
items: Geno Smith, QB. Brought in to stabilize the position, which for the Jets means simply being the same person taking snaps in December as in September.
QB battleBehind him, the competition between Bailey Zappe, former undrafted free agent Brady Cook and fourth-round rookie Cade Klubnik is described as the roster's biggest August focus.
David Bailey, EDGE (1st round). The headliner of a defensive rebuild that also brought in Ossai and Enagbare.
Kenyon Sadiq, TE & Omar Cooper Jr., WR (both 1st round). Two rookie pass catchers given every chance to start immediately.
D'Angelo Ponds, CB (2nd round). Pairs with free-agent Nahshon Wright in a reshaped secondary.
Depth is the actual goal. ESPN's framing of this camp is whether Mougey has added enough of it to create real competition — a low bar that the Jets have missed before.

right.title: Latest Roster Moves
head: Move
Detail
items: Signed after a season with the Raiders
Replaced along with half the staff

right.title: The Bottom Line
items: The Jets did what teams do when the roof is leaking in several rooms at once: replaced half the staff, spent three first-round picks on three different needs, and signed a veteran quarterback who has done this job well somewhere else. It is a coherent plan and it is probably a year early. Aaron Glenn is the one who can't afford it to be — his seat is the loudest storyline of a camp that otherwise carries modest expectations.

teams.sources: ESPN (2026 Jets training camp preview) · NewYorkJets.com · Newsweek · amNewYork · The Jet Press · Yahoo Sports.

teams.name: Eagles
teams.subhead: 2026 training camp edition — A.J. Brown is gone, the offense is being rebuilt around a new play-caller's vision, and every question routes back to Jalen Hurts.

left.title: Front Office & Leadership
items: New offensive voice. Sean Mannion, 34, formerly Green Bay's quarterbacks coach, is installing a scheme built on more under center, more motion, and more throws over the middle — concepts this offense has not leaned into with Hurts.

End of an era on the line. Jeff Stoutland, the offensive line coach since 2013 and the most respected position coach in the building, has departed. Chris Kuper takes over — this is the linemen's first camp under him.

Roseman kept trading. Philadelphia converted its best receiver into future capital and used the draft board aggressively again, extending the front office's pattern of selling a year early rather than a year late.

left.title: Trades & Major Transactions
items: TradeA.J. Brown to New England for a 2028 first-round pick and a 2027 fifth. From 2022–25 no NFL receiver commanded a greater share of his team's receiving yards (32.6%), and he was Hurts' safety valve against man coverage.
TradeAndy Dalton acquired from Carolina on a three-year, $24.75M deal ($15M guaranteed) — a serious investment in the backup room.
TradeSent S Sydney Brown and picks 122 and 215 to Atlanta for picks 114 and 197 (March 20).
SignedCB Riq Woolen — one year, up to $15M. WR Elijah Moore. RB Dameon Pierce (1 yr, March 19).
LostEDGE Jaelan Phillips to Carolina on a stunning 4-year, $120M deal; EDGE Azeez Ojulari to Atlanta; EDGE Josh Uche to Miami; QB Sam Howell to Dallas.

right.title: Player Updates & Camp Battles
items: Jalen Hurts, QB. The single biggest question in Philadelphia: whether his skill set and Mannion's under-center, middle-of-the-field vision actually align. Everything else on this roster is downstream of that answer.
Landon Dickerson, G. Traveled to Columbia for stem cell injections in his knees and ankles, hoping to buy a healthier 2026.
Cam Jurgens, C. Received stem cell treatment for back issues — the second of two starting interior linemen managing chronic problems.
Receiver room, reordered. With Brown traded and Elijah Moore added, the target hierarchy behind DeVonta Smith is genuinely unsettled going into camp.
Riq Woolen, CB. A one-year, high-upside bet on a corner whose traits have never been in question — the kind of prove-it deal Philadelphia has hit on before.
Edge rush, thinned out. Phillips, Ojulari and Uche all left in the same offseason. Replacing that rotation is the defense's central camp assignment.

right.title: Latest Roster Moves
head: Move
Detail
items: From Atlanta in the Sydney Brown swap
Traded to New England for a 2028 first

right.title: The Bottom Line
items: Philadelphia responded to a wild-card exit by changing the two things that had defined it: the receiver who bent defenses and the coach who built the offensive line. In their place is a first-time play-caller asking Jalen Hurts to run a different kind of offense, behind two interior starters seeking stem-cell relief, with an edge rotation that emptied out in free agency. Roseman banked a 2028 first for the trouble. Whether that reads as foresight or as a step back depends almost entirely on August.

teams.sources: ESPN (2026 Eagles training camp preview & free agency tracker) · PhiladelphiaEagles.com · NFL.com · PhillyVoice · Bleeding Green Nation · Sports Illustrated.

teams.name: Steelers
teams.subhead: 2026 training camp edition — Mike Tomlin is gone, Mike McCarthy is in, and Aaron Rodgers has announced this will be the last season of his career.

left.title: Front Office & Leadership
items: The end of the Tomlin era. Pittsburgh is in the middle of one of the most significant transitions in franchise history: Mike McCarthy officially takes over following Mike Tomlin's departure.

McCarthy and Rodgers, reunited. The two last worked together in Green Bay in 2017. McCarthy has told reporters Rodgers still has "otherworldly arm strength" — while the numbers show a career-low 5.8 air yards per attempt in 2025.
Nothing was left alone. Pittsburgh touched virtually every position group this offseason after another one-and-done postseason — bold trades, targeted free agency, and a clear draft priority.
The defense is the storyline that the sweeping changes were built around.

left.title: Trades & Major Transactions
items: SignedJamel Dean, CB — three years, $36.75M from Tampa Bay. He allowed a league-best 4.7 yards per target among outside corners in 2025.
SignedS Jaquan Brisker (1 yr / $5.5M, from Chicago, all 17 starts last season), S Darnell Savage, and DT Sebastian Joseph-Day — a defensive back seven rebuilt in one wave.
Offensive weapons in place: WRs DK Metcalf and Michael Pittman Jr., with a bruising backfield of Jaylen Warren and Rico Dowdle — the supporting cast assembled for Rodgers' last ride.
DraftQB Drew Allar in the third round (four-year rookie deal signed) and QB Will Howard in the sixth — the succession plan starts now.
RosterMason Rudolph remains on the roster, though how much longer is a fair question with two drafted quarterbacks in the room.

left.title: Rumor Mill
items: SpeculationNational voices have floated a T.J. Watt trade as part of a broader Steelers reset. There is no reported trade — but the contract friction underneath the chatter is real.

right.title: Player Updates & Camp Battles
items: ContractT.J. Watt, EDGE. Negotiations have not produced a new deal, and tension has grown into camp. Watt and Cam Heyward both missed practices or worked on their own this offseason while seeking more money.
How Watt is used. Pittsburgh may move him around more in 2026 to manufacture one-on-one matchups and reduce how often he's chipped.
Aaron Rodgers, QB. Season 22, and he has said it is his last. At 42 he is a different player than the one McCarthy coached — the offense will be built to hide that.
DK Metcalf & Michael Pittman Jr., WR. The best receiver pairing Rodgers has had in years.
Warren & Dowdle, RB. A deliberately physical backfield, designed to keep the passing game off schedule-neutral downs.
Drew Allar, QB. The third-rounder is the actual future; how much he shows in camp matters more than the depth chart says.

right.title: Latest Roster Moves
head: Move
Detail
items: Hired as head coach after Tomlin's departure

right.title: The Bottom Line
items: Pittsburgh replaced the second-longest-tenured coach in football, handed the job to the man who coached its 42-year-old quarterback a decade ago, and spent the offseason buying that quarterback the best supporting cast he has had since Green Bay. Rodgers says this is the end, which turns 2026 into a single-elimination season for everyone involved. The unresolved item is the best defensive player in the building: T.J. Watt wants paid, and camp starts anyway.

teams.sources: ESPN (2026 Steelers training camp preview & free agency tracker) · Newsweek · Steelers Depot · Behind the Steel Curtain · WTAJ · Sports Illustrated / All Steelers · Still Curtain.

teams.name: Seahawks
teams.subhead: 2026 training camp edition — defending Super Bowl LX champions, a fifth offensive coordinator in five years for Sam Darnold, and HBO cameras in the building.

left.title: Front Office & Leadership
items: Champions. Seattle beat New England 29–13 in Super Bowl LX at Levi's Stadium after a 14–3 regular season, then dispatched San Francisco 41–6 and the Rams 31–27 to get there.

New play-caller, familiar scheme. Rookie offensive coordinator Brian Fleury takes over — Darnold's fifth OC in five years — but is installing a system similar to Kubiak's, with new position coaches Jake Peetz and Tyson Prince alongside him.
Schneider's draft posture: the GM said openly the champions wanted to trade down — "it's no secret with us" — prioritizing volume over a single high pick.
Hard Knocks. A five-episode season debuts Aug. 4, featuring Macdonald, Darnold, 2025 Offensive Player of the Year Jaxon Smith-Njigba, Devon Witherspoon and Byron Murphy II.

left.title: Trades & Major Transactions
items: Re-signedRashid Shaheed, WR — three years, up to $51M. Seattle had acquired him in one of the biggest deals of the 2025 trade deadline; keeping him was the offseason's clearest priority.
SignedOLB Dante Fowler Jr. to bolster the edge rotation.
LostKenneth Walker III, RB — the Super Bowl MVP — departed in free agency, the most striking exit of any champion's offseason.
LostEDGE Boye Mafe, CB Riq Woolen (to Philadelphia) and S Coby Bryant (to Chicago) all found new homes.
Continuity where it counted: Darnold, Smith-Njigba, Witherspoon and Murphy II all return as the spine of the roster.

right.title: Player Updates & Camp Battles
items: Sam Darnold, QB. From first-round pick to journeyman backup to Pro Bowler to Super Bowl champion. The uncomfortable footnote: he led the NFL in turnovers during the regular season before playing clean football in the playoffs. Coaxing better decisions out of him is the coaching staff's stated task.
The OC carousel. Fleury is Darnold's fifth coordinator in five years. Scheme continuity with Kubiak's system is the mitigating factor.

Tory Horton, WR. The single biggest swing factor on offense. He caught five touchdowns in his first eight games as a rookie, then lost the rest of the season to a shin injury. Health decides how explosive this offense is.
Jaxon Smith-Njigba, WR. The reigning Offensive Player of the Year and the offense's non-negotiable.
Running back, wide open. Walker's departure leaves the Super Bowl MVP's carries unclaimed.
Secondary, reshuffled. Woolen and Bryant both left; Witherspoon and Murphy II now carry more.

right.title: Latest Roster Moves
head: Move
Detail
items: Super Bowl MVP departed in free agency

right.title: The Bottom Line
items: Seattle won a title and then watched its Super Bowl MVP running back, two starting defensive backs and an edge rusher walk out the door — the ordinary tax of a championship cap sheet. What stayed is the part that matters most: Macdonald's defense, Smith-Njigba, and a quarterback who finally has proof to point at. The repeat case rests on two things nobody can schedule — Tory Horton staying upright, and Darnold carrying his January decision-making into September.

teams.sources: ESPN (2026 Seahawks training camp preview) · Seahawks.com · Field Gulls · NFL.com · Wikipedia (2025 Seahawks season, 2025–26 playoffs) · Athlon Sports · Heavy.com.

teams.name: 49ers
teams.subhead: 2026 training camp edition — a veteran core coming off 50-plus missed starts, two new veteran receivers, and one question: is there enough left?

left.title: Front Office & Leadership
items: The premise of the offseason: health. San Francisco's starters missed a combined north of 50 games in 2025, systematically dismantling Shanahan's timing-based scheme before the season reached January.
The season ended 41–6 in the divisional round at Seattle — a result that framed every decision that followed.
The strategy: rather than rebuild, San Francisco bought proven veteran production at receiver and interior defensive line, betting the existing core plays.

QuestionNational previews put it directly: did the Niners do enough this offseason? Signing a 32-year-old receiver coming off an eight-game season is a departure from the youth-and-speed identity the front office had been building.

left.title: Trades & Major Transactions
items: SignedMike Evans, WR — three years, $60.4M, ending his 12-year run in Tampa Bay. Six-time Pro Bowler and Hall-of-Fame-track producer, but 32 and coming off an injury-plagued eight-game season.
TradeOsa Odighizuwa, DT acquired from Dallas for San Francisco's 2026 third-round pick — completed two days after the Evans signing.
SignedWR Christian Kirk — the intermediate-route complement to Evans, in a room that otherwise lacked proven options.
SignedOL Vederian Lowe (2 yr) and OL Brett Toth (1 yr) — depth for a line that has to protect better inside.
Re-signedTE Jake Tonges on a two-year deal.

right.title: Player Updates & Camp Battles
items: Brock Purdy, QB. Reported fine after the shoulder trouble that shaped his 2025. The whole offense's ceiling still runs through him.
Fred Warner, LB. Already cleared — the most encouraging health item on the board.
Nick Bosa, EDGE. Potentially back at the start of camp.
George Kittle, TE. Optimistic about a Week 1 return.
Left guard is the camp battle that matters. Interior pressure disrupted the 2025 offense more consistently than edge pressure did — and it lands directly on Purdy.
Mike Evans & Christian Kirk. Both must be synchronized with Purdy almost immediately; Shanahan's offense does not reward newcomers who need half a season.
Youth gets reps. With Kittle, Bosa and Warner all managing toward September rather than August, young players will see heavy camp volume — and some will win jobs.

Trade with Dallas for a 2026 third

right.title: The Bottom Line
items: San Francisco's 2025 was not a talent problem, it was an availability catastrophe — and the response was to add two veteran receivers and an interior rusher rather than reshape the roster. That works only if Bosa, Kittle, Warner and Purdy are all standing in January. The optimistic read is a Hall-of-Fame core with reinforcements. The pessimistic read is that the same core is a year older, a 32-year-old receiver is the marquee addition, and Seattle just put 41 on them. Left guard, of all things, may decide which one it is.

teams.name: Buccaneers
teams.subhead: 2026 training camp edition — Mike Evans is a 49er, Baker Mayfield still has no extension, and the deadline he set arrives July 28.

left.title: The Mayfield Standoff
items: No extension, and a hard line. Baker Mayfield publicly called Tampa Bay's initial offer disappointing, said he wants to stay long term, and stated he will not negotiate once training camp begins. The Bucs report July 28.
The number. Mayfield is seeking roughly $50M per year, the tier occupied by Brock Purdy and the league's other top-paid quarterbacks.
ReportedSI's Albert Breer says the Buccaneers are ready to "dive in" on negotiations and expects a long-term deal before Week 1 — which would mean blowing through Mayfield's own stated deadline.

The leverage math. Analysts have framed it plainly: the longer Tampa Bay waits, the more it likely pays. Despite an injury-filled, playoff-less 2025, the club still considers Mayfield its franchise quarterback.

left.title: Trades & Major Transactions
items: LostMike Evans, WR — the most decorated offensive player in franchise history signed a three-year, $60.4M deal with San Francisco. Bowles said the Bucs would have loved him back: "He knows how we feel about him, we think the world of him." Evans had earned the right to look.
LostJamel Dean, CB to Pittsburgh — three years, $36.75M. He allowed just 4.7 yards per target last season, the best mark in the NFL among outside corners, and was the glue of Bowles' secondary.
SignedLB Alex Anzalone, OLB Al-Quadin Muhammad and DL A'Shawn Robinson — depth-chart holes filled rather than headlines bought.
Re-signedNT Rakeem Nuñez-Roches; WR David Sills added on a one-year deal.
AssessmentNational grading of the offseason was blunt: depth signings can't paper over losing Evans and Dean in the same March.

right.title: Player Updates & Camp Battles
items: The receiver room is wide open. Bowles spent OTAs talking about competition at the position — with Evans gone, the depth chart behind the top returners is genuinely unsettled.
Zac Robinson's offense, Year 2. The coordinator's system continues to develop, and Bowles has emphasized execution in practice as the specific thing that has to improve.
Secondary, post-Dean. Replacing the league's most efficient outside corner is the defense's central problem; nobody on the roster has done that job at that level.
Alex Anzalone, LB. The most experienced addition, into a linebacker room that looks different from 2025.
Health first. The 2025 season was defined by injuries and ended without a playoff berth — availability, more than talent, is what Tampa Bay is trying to buy back.

right.title: The Bottom Line
items: Tampa Bay lost the best receiver in its history and the best cover corner in the league by yards per target in the same offseason, replaced them with depth signings, and now walks into camp with its quarterback publicly unhappy about an offer. July 28 is the date that matters — Mayfield says negotiations end when camp starts; the reporting says a deal lands before Week 1. One of those is wrong, and the answer sets the tone for the entire season.

teams.name: Titans
teams.subhead: 2026 training camp edition — a historic 3-14 meltdown triggers a massive overhaul, Robert Saleh takes over, and Cam Ward's development is everything.

left.title: Front Office & Leadership
items: Complete regime reset. Tennessee's 3-14 collapse in 2025 led to the mid-season firing of Brian Callahan and a complete overhaul, with Robert Saleh installed as the new head coach to salvage Cam Ward's career.

Go-all-in mentality. The Titans spent over $300M in free agency, adding more than 20 veteran players to reset the roster in a single offseason — an aggressive strategy that signals desperation and commitment.
Saleh's reputation on the line. Hired from his defensive coordinator role with San Francisco, Saleh must engineer a turnaround in Year 1 or face questions about his ability to lead.
Camp timeline: Rookies report July 23, veterans July 28.

left.title: Trades & Major Transactions
items: SignedWan'Dale Robinson, WR — four-year, $78M deal for a proven pass-catcher to support Ward.
TradeJermaine Johnson II, EDGE acquired from New York Jets to anchor the pass rush.
SignedFranklin-Myers, EDGE, Solomon Thomas, DT (trade), Taylor, CB, Flott, CB, and Daniel Bellinger, TE — veterans across the depth chart.
DraftedSupporting Ward's development: WR Carnell Tate, DE Keldric Faulk in first two rounds to surround the quarterback with playmakers.

right.title: Player Updates & Camp Battles
items: Cam Ward, QB. The focal point of every move this offseason. His development in Saleh's system, with real pass catchers and pass protection, will determine whether this rebuild works. This is his make-or-break moment in Year 2.
Wan'Dale Robinson, WR. Signed to be the #1 target and stabilizing presence for a sophomore quarterback who needs reliable options.
Robert Saleh's defense. The former 49ers DC brings a proven defensive philosophy; this unit should be far better than 2025's disaster.
Jermaine Johnson II, EDGE. Acquired to provide immediate pass-rush impact — the Titans need sacks and pressure around Ward.
The youth movement. Carnell Tate and Keldric Faulk were drafted to support Ward long-term, creating a young receiving and defensive core.

right.title: The Bottom Line
items: Tennessee threw everything at the 3-14 problem, spending over $300M to overhaul the roster in a single offseason. Robert Saleh arrives to engineer the turnaround, Cam Ward gets real weapons and protection, and Wan'Dale Robinson becomes his safety blanket. This is a team betting on aggressive veteran addition and coach change to salvage a sophomore quarterback who had every excuse to fail last year. If Saleh and Ward both thrive, this camp will be remembered as the turning point. If not, expect questions about whether this massive bet was the answer to the wrong question.

teams.name: Commanders
teams.subhead: 2026 training camp edition — two first-time coordinators, $100M spent on the edge, and a healthy Jayden Daniels asked to run a different offense.

left.title: Front Office & Leadership
items: Both coordinators replaced. Quinn promoted assistant QB coach David Blough to offensive coordinator (Kliff Kingsbury left for the Rams) and hired ex-Vikings pass game coordinator Daronte Jones as DC, replacing Joe Whitt Jr.

Two first-time NFL play-callers. Neither Blough nor Jones has called plays in the league; Jones has one year of coordinator experience at LSU. National coverage has framed these as genuine gambles — Quinn has publicly stood firm on both.
RumorQuinn's own seat. After a 5–12 collapse, hot-seat chatter has followed him into camp. A third straight uneven season with hand-picked, unproven coordinators would be difficult to explain.
The scheme shift. Blough's offense leans on more under-center play-action — a real departure from the shotgun-heavy attack Daniels ran as a rookie.

left.title: Trades & Major Transactions
items: SignedOdafe Oweh, EDGE — four years, $100M. The largest commitment of the offseason and the anchor of a rebuilt pass rush.
SignedDT Tim Settle Jr. (3 yr / $24M), LB Leo Chenal, S Nick Cross, CB Amik Robertson; EDGE Dorance Armstrong brought back.
SignedTE Chig Okonkwo and RB Rachaad White; WR Treylon Burks re-signed.
DraftWR Antonio Williams added to a receiver room that needed young legs.
LostWR Deebo Samuel allowed to walk after one season; RB Austin Ekeler not re-signed; TE Zach Ertz departed.

right.title: Player Updates & Camp Battles
items: Jayden Daniels, QB. The 2024 Offensive Rookie of the Year lost 2025 to a cascade of injuries — knee sprain, hamstring strain, and a dislocated elbow that ended his season. He played only four full games. Spring and summer reports have been encouraging: comfortable, moving well, back in sync with Terry McLaurin.
The adjustment. Daniels' transition to Blough's under-center, play-action-heavy system is the single most important variable in Washington's season.
Odafe Oweh, EDGE. $100M says the pass rush is now his responsibility. Paired with Armstrong and Settle inside, the front is unrecognizable from 2025.
Terry McLaurin, WR. Still the offense's anchor, and the chemistry reports with a healthy Daniels are the most positive signal out of the spring.
Receiver room, reset. With Samuel gone, rookie Antonio Williams and re-signed Treylon Burks compete for snaps behind McLaurin.
Backfield, reset. Rachaad White replaces Ekeler as the veteran presence.

head: Move
Detail

Allowed to leave after one season

right.title: The Bottom Line
items: Washington's 2025 was a health story disguised as a collapse — four full games from Jayden Daniels and a 5–12 finish. The fix was money on defense (Oweh's $100M leading a rebuilt front) and a philosophical reset on offense. The risk is concentrated in one place: Dan Quinn handed both play-calling jobs to men who have never held them in the NFL, in a year his own seat is being discussed. A healthy Daniels makes it look bold. Anything less makes it look like the last decision he gets to make.
